recent_facts.fact: The most recent independent general-election polls had Democrat Rob Sand ahead of Republican Zach Lahn. NYT/Siena (Sep 22–Oct 1): Sand 52%, Lahn 41%. Fox News (Sep 24–28): Sand 53%, Lahn 44%.
A Marist poll of 1,050 Iowa registered voters taken Sep 17–20, 2026 had Sand at 54% and Lahn at 42%.

Other September polls also had Sand ahead. YouGov (Sep 3–8): 51–41. Emerson (Aug 31–Sep 1): 49–46. Cygnal (Sep 9–11, 500 likely voters): about 48–44.4. Rasmussen (Sep 8–10, 1,031 likely voters): 50–39. The Republican-aligned firm co/efficient (Sep 14–16, 831 likely voters): 46–42.

Zach Lahn, a businessman and farmer, won the June 2 Republican primary and U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra conceded. Rob Sand was unopposed for the Democratic nomination. Gov. Kim Reynolds is not running again, so the seat is open.
Three candidates are on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot: Rob Sand (D), Zach Lahn (R) and Libertarian Nicholas Gluba.

The first gubernatorial debate was held Oct 6, 2026 at St. Ambrose University in Davenport. Sand raised Lahn's Kansas residency, saying Iowa needs a 'full-time Iowan' as governor. Lahn criticized data centers and focused on agriculture.
Four debates are scheduled before Election Day on November 3, 2026, and the first took place Oct 6.
Sand is campaigning for support beyond the Democratic base. The polling coverage cited above credits much of his lead to independent voters.

In 2024 the final Des Moines Register/Selzer Iowa Poll had Harris ahead by 3 points, but Trump won Iowa by about 13.2 points. That was a miss of more than 16 points in the Republican direction. The Register's Iowa Poll has since been discontinued.

In 2020, Sen. Joni Ernst trailed by just under 3 points on average across 19 tracked polls, then won by 6.6 points. Trump led Iowa's final five polls by about 2 points on average and won by 8.5. Polls also underestimated Ernst in 2014.
Trump has won Iowa three times, most recently by 13+ points in 2024. From memory and unverified here: Republicans have won the last four Iowa governor races (2010, 2014, 2018, 2022).

The question resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate. If they don't, it resolves on official certification. The Republican option is whoever is the GOP nominee, currently Zach Lahn.

recent_facts.fact: As of Oct 4, 2026, an average of six polling aggregators showed Republican Gov. Greg Abbott at 48.5% and Democrat Gina Hinojosa at 46.7%, so Abbott was ahead by 1.8 points.
YouGov (Sept 28–Oct 5, 3,625 likely voters, ±3.0) had Hinojosa 48% and Abbott 47%. NYT/Siena (Sept 22–Oct 1, 615 likely voters) had Hinojosa 49% and Abbott 46%.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (polls listed: Beacon Research/Shaw & Co., Stratus Intelligence)
recent_facts.fact: Beacon Research/Shaw & Co. (Sept 24–28, 1,005 likely voters) had Abbott 52% and Hinojosa 47%. Stratus Intelligence (Sept 22–24, 865 likely voters) had Abbott 50% and Hinojosa 45%. Texas Public Opinion Research (Aug 21–24) had Abbott 49% and Hinojosa 42%.

A ReconMR/Siena poll from Sept 18 had Hinojosa ahead 49–45. The same firm had Abbott up by 1 in July, so that is a 5-point swing. A late-September Marist poll had Hinojosa ahead 49–46. Abbott launched a $12M ad accusing Hinojosa of voting 40 times to raise taxes, and data centers have become a major issue in rural counties.

No debate between Abbott and Hinojosa is scheduled. Hinojosa says she has accepted four TV debate invitations, and Abbott has not responded. Abbott did debate in each of his previous governor races (2014, 2018, 2022).
Abbott publicly downplayed the tight polls and took new steps against data centers, the issue that has become central to the race.

Abbott started 2026 with $105.7M cash on hand after raising $22.7M in the second half of 2025. Hinojosa raised $1.3M in the last 10 weeks of 2025. Abbott said he would spend most of his roughly $90M in Harris County.

In the March 3 primaries, Abbott won the Republican nomination with 81.8% (1,764,924 votes) and Hinojosa won the Democratic nomination with 58.5% (1,289,576 votes). Libertarian Pat Dixon is also on the ballot and polled at 3% in a University of Houston survey.

Early voting in Texas starts Oct 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov 3, 2026. The question closes Nov 4 at 04:59 UTC. It resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race; if they don't all agree, it goes by official certification.

Republicans have won every Texas governor race since 1994, which is 8 in a row (1994–2022). The last Democrat to win was Ann Richards in 1990. Abbott won in 2022 by 10.9 points (54.75% to 43.86%) and in 2018 by 13.3 points.
In 2020, the final RealClearPolitics average in Texas had Trump up only 1 point. He won 52% to 46%, so polls understated his share by a little over 4 points.

In 2024, Quinnipiac, Morning Consult and Emerson showed a tied presidential race in Texas, but Trump won 56.2% to 42.4%. Cruz beat Allred 53% to 44.6%. Republicans running better than the polls in more years than these two is the desk's recollection only (unverified).

market.question: Will Trump speak to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual speaks with Donald Trump between market creation and October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Speaking is defined as any verbal interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.

The resolution source will be credible media reporting. However, in the absence of definitive or in the case of contradictory media reporting, statements by either of the specified individuals or their official representatives will also be considered.

Statements by the specified individuals or their official representatives will only be considered conclusive if the claims explicitly, or in context unambiguously, indicate that a qualifying talk occurred within the specified timeframe and took place via verbal communication, and provided that such claims are not contradicted by the other specified individual, their representatives, or credible media reporting by the end of the third calendar date (ET) following the statement in question.

This market will resolve at the earlier of i) a qualifying verbal interaction being confirmed under the above rules or ii) 11:59 PM ET on the third calendar day following this market's above-specified timeframe.

If the date and time of a qualifying talk cannot be confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting by 11:59 PM ET on the third calendar day following this market's above-specified timeframe, it will resolve to "No" regardless of whether it was later confirmed to have taken place.
